ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the French PEP definition (Article L.561-10 CMF), the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, and Tracfin (French FIU) suspicious-transaction typologies; screening is performed prior to incorporation and on a continuous basis. A U.S. OFAC/SDN sanctions check is additionally performed as a prudential standard because the target payment rails (Apple IAP and Google Play Billing) require U.S. platform compliance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe (RCS national database) and INPI Data (data.inpi.fr); creation filings are submitted via the official formalities hub at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SARL denomination may be in any Latin-script language; if a foreign script is used, the articles must show a literal transliteration into the Latin alphabet. The RCS registers the transliterated Latin form, and the name must be freely available, not contrary to public order, and not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company name or trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name rejection is notified by the Greffe with reasons. The applicant may resubmit a revised name with a supporting note under Article R.123-54 of the French Commercial Code, or, where the rejection is based on prior infringement or public-order grounds, apply to the Président du Tribunal de Commerce in summary proceedings (référé) and then appeal to the Cour d'appel within one month of the notification. All INPI/Infogreffe search reports must be attached to rebut identity-confusion objections.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited permissibility: a domiciliation office (agence de domiciliation) may be used for RCS registration, but tax authorities may apply substance-over-form review. For a digital subscription platform, a virtual office is accepted during inception only if supported by a local registered agent, a French corporate bank account, and a local compliance file.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% annual probability in the first three fiscal years for an online content publisher with no physical inventory; the risk rises to approximately 15% if UBO declarations are delayed, payment flows are routed through non-European aggregators, or the APE code (9000Z) does not match the actual editorial and publishing activity.

RESOLUTION OF THE PROPOSED BOARD OF DIRECTORS
The directors of the proposed Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) hereby unanimously adopt the following resolutions: 1. The initial share capital of the Company shall be set at one euro (1 EUR) and shall be fully subscribed by the founding shareholders, who shall execute the corresponding share subscription agreements. 2. industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing authority required for digital content platform

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; principal portals are impots.gouv.fr and the professional tax account (espace professionnel). Business formation and statutory registration filings are submitted through the INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises. The competent local tax office is generally the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is registered through the INPI Guichet unique before commencing business. The filing produces a SIREN identifier for the entity and a SIRET identifier for each establishment. The DGFiP then assigns or confirms the French VAT identification number, generally formatted as FR plus a two-character key and the nine-digit SIREN. The entity must provide formation documents, registered-office evidence, corporate identity information, beneficial-owner information, business activity details, bank and accounting information, and the expected date and nature of taxable transactions. A foreign entity without a French establishment applies to the competent French non-established-business tax service for a French VAT number before making transactions requiring French VAT registration. EU-established businesses may use the competent tax administration or applicable EU procedures; non-EU businesses may be required to appoint a French fiscal representative unless an applicable treaty or administrative arrangement removes that requirement. VAT registration does not itself establish a French permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). Certain SARLs may elect corporate-income-tax transparency and taxation at shareholder level (impôt sur le revenu, IR), including qualifying family SARLs and, subject to statutory conditions, qualifying newly established SARLs. The ordinary qualifying SARL election is time-limited, while the family-SARL regime can continue while eligibility conditions are satisfied. France has no general US-style check-the-box election for SARLs. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implementing ATAD 2 can deny deductions or require inclusion for specified hybrid arrangements; they are statutory anti-avoidance rules rather than elective entity-classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), including domestic French VAT, the Union One Stop Shop (OSS), and the Import One Stop Shop (IOSS) where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business providing services, the principal franchise en base de TVA threshold is EUR 37,500 of annual turnover, with a EUR 41,250 tolerance threshold under the applicable rules. The applicable thresholds differ for goods and certain regulated activities. A business may elect to become VAT-liable before exceeding the franchise threshold. There is generally no French turnover threshold for a non-established business making French VAT-taxable supplies that require French registration. For qualifying intra-EU cross-border B2C telecommunications, broadcasting and electronically supplied services, the EUR 10,000 EU-wide annual threshold may apply before destination-country taxation and OSS obligations arise. Apple and Google platform collection does not automatically eliminate the SARL's VAT obligations; the contractual principal, merchant-of-record status, commission model and customer location must be determined.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting through approved private platforms connected to the public directory. From 1 September 2026, all businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices; large and mid-sized businesses must generally issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from that date. Small and medium-sized businesses must generally issue them from 1 September 2027. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. France's model is not a universal real-time VAT clearance system: domestic B2B e-invoicing and e-reporting will transmit prescribed invoice and transaction data to the tax administration, while cross-border and B2C transactions are generally handled through e-reporting and applicable OSS or other VAT procedures. Electronic invoices must contain required French and EU VAT data, structured invoice fields, identity and VAT-number information, transaction dates, tax bases, rates and amounts, and reliable authenticity and integrity controls.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the EU are generally VAT-exempt with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU and the exporter can prove export and exit through customs evidence. Intra-EU supplies of goods may be VAT-exempt with the right to deduct where the customer has a valid VAT number in another Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and the supplier retains the required proof and makes required recapitulative declarations. Services are not automatically zero-rated: B2B services are generally taxed where the business customer is established, subject to special rules, and B2C electronically supplied services are generally taxed where the consumer resides. A French digital reading platform must analyze customer location, customer status, app-store contractual roles, OSS eligibility and any marketplace deemed-supplier rule. Input VAT refunds require valid invoices, customs records and evidence that the underlying supplies qualify for deduction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French or EU customs export declaration, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Electronic proof of exit or customs confirmation that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, consignee, goods, value, destination and contractual terms
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note or equivalent carrier evidence
Packing list and, where applicable, export licence, certificate of origin and product-specific regulatory documents
Accounting records linking the export declaration, invoice, shipment and VAT return
For qualifying services: contract, customer-status evidence, customer-location evidence, service records and payment documentation
An inward remittance certificate is not generally a mandatory French export-VAT document; bank evidence may support payment and transaction substantiation but does not replace customs proof of exit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general foreign-exchange control rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. Export proceeds should nevertheless be recorded, collected and reconciled under ordinary accounting, anti-money-laundering, customs and transfer-pricing controls. If export exemption or an input-VAT refund is unsupported, the DGFiP may retrospectively reassess output VAT, deny or claw back input-VAT credits and refunds, and charge late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month under the French Tax Code. Penalties may include 5% for certain filing or payment failures, 40% for deliberate non-compliance, and up to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abusive conduct, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards. False customs declarations can trigger customs duties, VAT, customs penalties and, in serious cases, criminal proceedings. Documentation must be retained for the applicable French accounting, VAT and customs limitation periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France); Foreign Exchange Administration de facto delegated to the Direction Générale du Trésor under the Code Monétaire et Financier (Articles L151-1 et seq.)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member state; the EUR is fully convertible with no exchange control approvals required for current account payments. Capital account transactions are broadly liberalised but subject to statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the Banque de France when any single cross-border transaction exceeds EUR 15,000 (excluding inter-EU flows). Dividend and profit remittances by a SARL to its shareholders are freely transferable; French withholding tax may apply for non-EU shareholders unless reduced under a tax treaty, and EU parent-subsidiary directive protection applies for qualifying EU corporate shareholders. No administrative FX licence is required for conversion from EUR to foreign currency for trade or investment purposes, provided the underlying activity is lawful and compliant with anti-money-laundering obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. French law imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio for export proceeds (including digital services revenue). The SARL may retain USD, EUR, or other freely convertible currencies in its treasury accounts. However, for national statistics, export proceeds attributed to French residents must be declared to the Banque de France within the annual balance-of-payments filing when they exceed the EUR 15,000 threshold per calendar year. App-store gross settlements (Apple/Google) are booked as export of digital services and must be traceable in the statutory accounting records.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Cash Concentration Account
Operational Account; Capital Escrow possible upon request for acquisition funding
Operational Account; Escrow Account for regulated equity only

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for day-to-day operational treasury through French-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto or Shine. Legal constraints: these are ACPR-regulated payment institutions under PSD2; they may hold client funds, execute SEPA and SWIFT transfers, and issue payment cards, but may not grant credit or hold escrowed capital at long tenor. Offshore non-EU EMIs are not permitted to provide payment services into France absent an EU branch or licence passported under PSD2; hence the SARL should maintain at least one Tier-1 bank account for statutory capital, dividends, and tax payments. An EMI may be used for app-store recovery settlement and FX conversion only when the payout is legally attributable to the SARL and the EMI performs strict KYB.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under French AML law (Articles L561-5 et seq. of the Code Monétaire et Financier), a bank may conduct full remote onboarding using qualified electronic identification and video verification; no statutory obligation exists for a director to appear physically. However, most Tier-1 banks, for a non-resident beneficial owner of a digital-web-fiction SARL, will require one in-branch sign-off for the signature card and final sanctioning of the account opening, unless the bank accepts a notarised power of attorney supplemented by an apostille and certified passport copies. Remote onboarding is permitted where the beneficial owner is already banked in the same banking group or where the commercial risk is low. Directors resident outside the EU must provide a consular or apostilled proof of identity and a non-resident tax declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: WebNovel app with no audited financial history and intangible-only assets; bank classifies as 'higher AML risk' due to low transparency of platform revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the SARL incorporation deed and statutes (K-bis extract); notarised director's identity documents (passport/ID); sworn statement of beneficial ownership; ISIC 9000/NAICS 511130 business description; INPI registration of the trademark or the website/domain particulars; Apple Developer Program agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement; current app-store monetary reports showing net billing; historical payout statements from Apple/Google; domiciliation contract or asset-backed lease proving French physical footprint; shareholder loan agreement and source-of-wealth statement for injected capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Voluminous cross-border settlement from Apple/Google in USD routed via auxiliary payment accounts, obscuring beneficial flow.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The 'dossier de conformité' with a statement of treasury flows charting the payment path: end-user IAP transaction to Apple/Google net settlement to the SARL; the bank's current account statement showing consistent credits; export proceeds declaration history to Banque de France; a copy of the platform's user-subscription terms; and an internal export-invoice schedule reconciled to the monthly payouts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder(s) remitting start-up capital in a single lump sum without proof of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of foreign bank statements of the contributing shareholder; source-of-funds certificate executed by the shareholder's overseas bank; signed minutes of capital increase; proof of discharge of the contribution through SWIFT MT103; certified copies of passport of ultimate beneficial owner; tax residential certificate or CRS declaration; declaration to the Banque de France of the inward capital movement if above EUR 15,000.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: use SWIFT MT103 in EUR to the SARL's French euro account. For EU shareholders, standard SEPA Credit Transfer is sufficient. The bank reference field must state 'Capital Increase - SARL Apport en Numéraire' and identify the share register reference; the purpose code for French balance-of-payments reporting is 'Capital transfer – equity participation or subscription'. The bank must receive: a certified extract of the company registry, minutes of the extraordinary general meeting resolving the capital increase, shareholder list, and a decomposition of the contribution amount. The contribution is held in the statutory capital account and cannot be swept without a further formal act; the bank will verify that the inbound funds originate from the shareholder declared in the KYC file, not a third party. For amounts above EUR 15,000, the SARL, through the bank, must file the French balance-of-payments statistical form (CERFA equivalent) with the Direction Générale du Trésor.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (1) EU and EEA author royalties, licensor fees, and refunds: SEPA Credit Transfer (instant or delayed) using IBAN/BIC, with no FX cost. (2) Non-EU content licensing, author royalties, platform development, and operational invoices: SWIFT MT103 in the settlement currency, with the beneficiary bank routed through correspondents; for volume payments (e.g., Russian, Indian, Brazilian authors), a single MT103 with a structured remittance advice can be batched through the treasury, but each underlying contract and tax withholding certificate must be retained. (3) Commercial LC (documentary credit) is permissible but unusual for webnovel royalties; it is reserved for large-scale IP acquisitions (e.g., film/TV adaptation licenses) where the issuing bank in France may open a confirmed LC in favour of the non-EU licensor. (4) App-store refunds and chargebacks traverse the acquiring rails (Stripe/Adyen/Apple/Google) and appear as reversals against the SARL's funding account; this does not require a separate clearing rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX forward contract for hedging monthly Apple and Google payout receipts in USD into EUR
EUR/USD and EUR/GBP FX Swaps (swap and forward combined) for liquidity bridging among treasury accounts
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) for INR, IDR, TRY, PHP, and similar non-convertible emerging-market currencies arising from content royalties or app-store remittances, settled in EUR
European-style FX options (calls/puts) on EUR/USD for contingent app-store settlement exposure, subject to bank approval and ISDA/CSA documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting / written shareholders' consultation approving the annual financial statements and allocation of result
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; minutes recorded in statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government fine, but any interested shareholder may petition the Tribunal de Commerce to convene the meeting; managers remain civilly liable for losses caused by failure to hold the meeting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of approved annual accounts with the commercial registry (dépôt des comptes annuels au RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, submitted via Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of fiscal year-end and no later than 1 month after shareholder approval, whichever is earlier; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the effective outer deadline falls on 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice by the court registrar; mandatory filing order in the event of continued failure; possible fine for managers up to EUR 3,000 and daily coercive fine (astreinte); persistent non-compliance can lead to administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, Cerfa 2065 and annexes) including income statement and balance sheet as filed for corporate tax purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending 31 December: by the second business day after 1 May of the following year; for any other fiscal year-end: within 3 months after close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of corporate income tax due, increased to 10% after a formal notice; late payment interest of 0.40% per month; ex officio assessment by the tax administration; potential criminal fine up to EUR 1,500 for repeated failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner declaration annual confirmation and update following any transfer of shares or changes in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés via Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation is made with the annual accounts filing and no later than 7 months after fiscal year-end; any change arising from a share transfer must be declared within 30 days after the transfer is legally completed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the beneficial owner register obligation is a criminal offence: up to 6 months' imprisonment and EUR 30,000 fine for responsible managers; company may also face administrative barriers, RCS warnings, and civil liability; continued non-filing may contribute to forced RCS strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual internal audit and the maintenance of statutory registers and corporate records (share register, transfer records, minutes, UBO register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance; registers must be kept available for inspection by the RCS clerk, tax authorities, and judicial authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the annual general meeting and prior to the RCS filing, as part of the annual close; records must be continuously updated throughout the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or non-maintained statutory registers expose the managers to a contravention fine of up to EUR 6,000 and may create evidentiary weakness in litigation; failure to produce registers upon official request may trigger criminal sanctions and corporate strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux comptes) is triggered when the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at fiscal year-end: total balance sheet exceeding EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding tax exceeding EUR 8,000,000; and average number of employees exceeding 50. Additionally, an auditor may be appointed voluntarily by shareholders or appointed by court order upon request of a shareholder group.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts of a French SARL must be prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, PCG, applying ANC Regulation 2014-03, as amended and currently consolidated by the ANC 2016-06 framework). IFRS as endorsed by the EU is required only for consolidated financial statements of listed groups and is not required for a standalone SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the French Monetary and Financial Code, the SARL must keep a permanent and updated register of beneficial owners. The declaration of beneficial owners is filed with the RCS on incorporation and must be renewed whenever there is a change; at each annual accounts filing, the company confirms that the filed beneficial-owner information remains accurate. For share transfers, the updated beneficial-owner declaration is due within 30 days after completion of the transfer and must reflect the new percentage of ownership and control. The annual confirmation is not a separate standalone form but is aligned with the annual RCS accounts filing.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – USD 2,000 per annum depending on city, provider, and level of legal assistance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 28,000 per audit engagement for a typical small-to-mid-size SARL; engagements involving consolidated accounts, IFRS, or complex intercompany structures will be priced above the upper bound

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced effective rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for eligible small enterprises with turnover below EUR 10 million; additional R&D tax credit (CIR) at 30% up to EUR 100 million and 5% above may apply for eligible digital content development.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward (no statutory expiry); annual taxpayer offset limited to EUR 1 million plus 50% of remaining taxable income in excess of the EUR 1 million threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 2065-SD (annual income tax return) with supporting schedules 2053 to 2069; filed electronically via the French tax authority portal 'impots.gouv.fr' through the Téléprocédures EDI-TDFC service.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return must be filed by 15 May of the following calendar year. For non-calendar fiscal year-ends, the return is due within 60 days after the close of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying loss carryforwards, deductions, and fiscal adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an SARL with non-resident shareholders, this box reflects only the entity-level corporate income tax base; shareholding residency has no effect on this field, but proper attribution of dividends must be documented for withholding tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits available against corporate income tax, including research and innovation credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may not carry tax credits of the entity; credits apply solely to the SARL and must be substantiated by supporting forms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss carryforwards and current-year deficit absorption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward positions are part of the French entity's fiscal history and are unaffected by ownership residency, but change-of-control anti-abuse limitations apply under Article 221bis CGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional 3% social contribution for companies with taxable income above a statutory threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This charge is computed at entity level; no non-resident shareholder filing requirement arises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% penalty of the tax due plus 0.75% per month late-payment interest; for non-filing after formal notice, ex officio assessment with a 100% surcharge may apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 2571-SD (advance corporate tax payments) and Form No. 2573-SD (balance payment); remitted electronically through impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly advance instalments with an annual balance payment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly instalments due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December; final balance due with the annual return on the applicable deadline described for Form 2065-SD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reference corporate income tax base from the preceding fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For newly established SARLs, the first-year instalment base is calculated on the total corporate income tax estimated for the first fiscal year; non-resident shareholders must ensure cash-flow planning for such prepayments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly prepayment amount reflecting the prior-year tax, with possible inter-period reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax reductions or exemptions must be validly claimed by the SARL; foreign shareholders cannot claim a refund of the entity's prepayments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Case C — Imputation des crédits d'impôt
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offsetting of tax credits against the instalment due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No direct application to non-resident shareholders; any excess credit after balance may be carried forward or refunded to the French entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment penalty of 5% on the unpaid amount plus monthly 1.2% late-payment interest; inadequate instalments may trigger fixed penalties and administrative surcharges.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on gross dividends paid by a French SARL to non-resident corporate and individual shareholders (CGI art. 119 bis-2), plus a 3% social contribution on distributions borne by the distributing company (CGI art. 235 ter ZCA).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must, at or before the time of distribution, provide to the paying French SARL a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home tax authority, and, for reduced treaty rates, file a simplified application with the French tax authority (Form 5000 for income tax and Form 5001 for fiscal residence application). For the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, a parent company owning at least 10% of the SARL for a continuous two-year period may claim 0% withholding on dividends by presenting a holding declaration and a TRC; anti-abuse conditions apply under the French substance and purpose test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding rate of 33.33% on French-source royalty payments to non-residents (CGI art. 182 B); under the France–Luxembourg DTA, royalties of literary and artistic copyright may be exempt from French withholding if the beneficial owner is resident in Luxembourg. Interest: in general, no French statutory withholding tax on loan interest paid to non-residents unless the borrower falls under anti-tax-haven or abusive-payment provisions; France–Luxembourg DTA allocates taxation of interest to Luxembourg, yielding a 0% French source rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File and Local File documentation is required for French entities belonging to a multinational group with consolidated turnover of or above EUR 750 million. For entities below this threshold, transfer pricing documentation may still be requested by the tax administration during an audit if cross-border controlled transactions are material and lack an arm's-length justification.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code as in UAE. Instead, French tax law applies a substance-over-form doctrine under the abuse of law provision (LPF art. L. 64) and general anti-abuse principles. An SARL with no actual management, premises, personnel, or risks in France may be disregarded for tax purposes or found to be an artificial arrangement lacking economic substance, especially in relation to royalty flows and treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of French-source subscription revenue generated by the web novel platform, concealment of Apple IAP / Google Play Billing earnings, or use of an offshore shell to redirect profit without operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Up to 80% penalty on evaded tax for abuse of law, and 40% penalty for intentional misstatement; criminal fine up to EUR 750,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years for aggravated tax fraud (CGI art. 1741). The tax administration may also order the closure of the entity and publication of sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors sign the corporate tax return and may be individually prosecuted for fraud; courts may pierce the corporate veil, order civil restitution of evaded taxes and interest, impose travel bans, issue disbarment from management, and sentence the director to up to 7 years' imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an SARL that has no genuine business purpose, no physical presence, no employees, and functions solely to hold web novel IP rights or to route subscription revenues in order to obtain French tax advantages or treaty benefits without real economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may disregard the entity under the abuse of law procedure, reassess profits in the hands of the real beneficial owner, and impose an 80% penalty plus late-payment interest of 4.8% per annum; also potential criminal sanctions for tax evasion if fraud is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may be held jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt; French law permits protective seizure of personal assets, and the commercial court may order a director's personal bankruptcy (faillite personnelle) with a management ban of up to 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Beneficial Ownership Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify the beneficial owner of the SARL with the French Trade Registry, non-declaration of foreign bank accounts used for Apple IAP / Google Play collections, absence of client due diligence for the digital platform, or deliberate concealment of cryptocurrency or foreign payment settlement accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 500,000 for breach of AML and beneficial ownership obligations; criminal sanctions under the French Monetary and Financial Code of up to 5 years' imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine for laundering the proceeds of tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted personally for AML violations; courts may order liquidation of the entity, asset confiscation, travel bans, and imprisonment; directors can also be removed from office under judicial decision.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging artificial royalties or service fees to a foreign related party without arm's length justification, failure to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, or failing to file the annual transfer pricing declaration for the French web novel platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment by the French tax administration, plus a 40% penalty for lack of documentation or deliberate misstatement, and up to 80% for abusive situations; fixed late-payment surcharge of 1.2% per month may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the tax declaration certifying a deficient transfer pricing policy can be held jointly liable for the reassessed tax, subject to personal tax penalties, and in serious cases criminal prosecution for tax evasion with travel bans and imprisonment.
